issues.source_quote: Нам не страшен серый волк, серый волк, серый волк...
issues.translation_quote: Who's afraid of the big gray wolf, big gray wolf, big gray wolf...
issues.justification: Replaces the Russian children's song with a different well-known English song; this is a plausible domestication, but the following 'Я злой и страшный серый волк' rhyme is rewritten and the reference is approximated.

issues.translation_quote: I'll rip your jaw off! / gouge your peepers out!
issues.justification: Catchphrase threat is rendered inconsistently ('jaw'/'jaws', 'peepers'), and 'Docent' speech loses the gangster idiom 'пасть' (maw/trap), weakening the recurring joke.
The slang 'редиска' (a bad sort) is kept literally, so the running joke is opaque; later 'Take back the radish!' and 'Answer for the radish' lose sense in English.

issues.source_quote: Сколько я зарезал, сколько перерезал, сколько душ я загубил!
issues.translation_quote: How many have I slaughtered, how many have I butchered, how many souls have I destroyed!
issues.justification: This is a parody of a famous theatrical/song line; the comic pastiche register is only roughly conveyed.

issues.source_quote: Какой же это арматурный, это слесарный. Чего ты свистишь?
issues.justification: Plausible, but 'свистишь' (lying) fits the criminal slang; minor shift. Also 'Alibakan' character speech is inconsistent.

issues.translation_quote: It's gone. It was here, now it's not.
issues.justification: Ali-Baba's pidgin and Sanych's lines are mixed up; speaker voices are blurred.
